title: Suspected Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT)
vignette: A 45-year-old female presents to the urgent care clinic with left calf swelling and pain that started 2 days ago. She recently returned from a long-haul flight. She has no active cancer, no previous DVT, and her vital signs are normal, apart from localized tenderness along the deep venous system. Her left calf is 4cm larger than her right, measured 10cm below the tibial tuberosity.
educationalRationale: According to NICE (NG158), the first step in suspected DVT is a 2-level Wells score. Her score would be 2 (calf swelling >3cm = 1, tenderness = 1). Since Wells is 'Likely' (≥ 2), the correct immediate action is to arrange a proximal leg vein ultrasound, and offer interim therapeutic anticoagulation if the scan cannot be done within 4 hours.

title: New-onset Atrial Fibrillation
vignette: A 72-year-old male with a history of hypertension and Type 2 Diabetes is found to have an irregular pulse during a routine review. An ECG confirms Atrial Fibrillation. He has no history of stroke or TIA and his recent blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg.
educationalRationale: NICE NG196 recommends assessing stroke risk using CHA2DS2-VASc for all patients with AF. This patient scores at least 3 (Age 65-74 = 1, Hypertension = 1, Diabetes = 1). Since the score is ≥2, anticoagulation with a DOAC should be offered.

title: Community-Acquired Pneumonia
vignette: A 68-year-old male presents with a 4-day history of productive cough, fever (38.5°C), and shortness of breath. His respiratory rate is 26 breaths/min, oxygen saturation is 96% on air, and blood pressure is 110/65 mmHg. He is alert and oriented. He has a history of mild asthma.
educationalRationale: NICE CG191 recommends using the CRB-65 or CURB-65 score in primary care to assess pneumonia severity. This patient scores 1 (Age ≥ 65 = 1, no confusion, RR < 30, BP normal). Score = 1 indicates low/intermediate risk, usually suitable for home-based antibiotic therapy (e.g., Amoxicillin 500mg TDS).
